article.body_html:
A new job, a new commute and no idea whether a motorbike is the right way to do it: a week's rental looks like the cautious choice, with a monthly rental to follow if it works. The risk is that the week turns out to be an expensive way of finding out, because nobody agreed in advance whether the first week counts towards the month. A good trial answers two questions, whether the bike suits the commute and what the switch to a monthly rental will cost, and it is set up so that both answers are in hand by the end of the sixth day.

What a week needs to prove

A trial is only as good as what you test. Make a short list on the first day and tick items off as the week goes by.

  • The real commute at the real hours. Ride the route at the times you will ride it every day, not on a quiet Sunday. A road that is easy at 11:00 can be a different road at the end of the working day.
  • The parking at both ends. Check where the bike will stand at home and at work, and whether it can be locked there.
  • The bike type. Manual and automatic bikes feel different in slow traffic, and a week shows which one you would want for a month.
  • Comfort over time. A bike that feels fine on a short test ride can feel different after several daily rides with a bag on your back.
  • Fuel and running costs. A fuel log started on day one gives you a figure to budget with.
  • A rainy day, if the week gives you one. You cannot choose the weather, and you do not have to ride in heavy rain for the trial to count. If you do ride on wet roads, go slowly and note how the bike and the route feel.

A week laid out day by day

DayWhat to doWhat to decide or ask
1Check the bike before you ride, photograph it and start the fuel logAsk the shop how the first week can turn into a monthly rental, before the week begins
2–3Ride the commute at your real hours, once in each directionNote any point on the route that worries you
4Park where you would park for a monthIs there a safe place to leave the bike overnight?
5Ride at the busiest hour of your real commute; if the roads are wet, ride only if you feel confident, and slow downIs this still the right size and type of bike?
6Add up the fuel and decideMessage the shop with your decision and check the answers you were given about the switch
7Return the bike, or carry on into the month as agreedGet the new dates, rate and deposit position in writing

The trial runs more smoothly if the shop knows it is a trial. How to check the bike before you ride shows what to look at on day one.

Questions about turning the week into a month

The shop sets the terms, and its answers may differ from what you expect. Ask all of these at the start, so that day six is for deciding and not for finding out the rules.

  1. Does the first week count towards the month, or does a new monthly rental start when the week ends?
  2. Which rate applies to the days after the week: the weekly rate, the monthly rate or something else?
  3. Is the week's payment credited towards the month in any way?
  4. Will I keep the same bike, and what happens to the deposit I have already paid?
  5. When must I tell you my decision for the switch to be smooth, and how should I tell you?
  6. If I decide the bike does not suit me, how do I return it at the end of the week?

If the shop treats the switch as an extension of the rental you already have, the guide to extending a rental lists what to confirm.

What the trial may cost

Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà gives reference prices for a manual bike of 700,000 to 800,000 VND for a week and 1,000,000 to 1,200,000 VND for a month. For illustration, if a week were charged in full and a separate month followed at the monthly reference price, the two together would come to 1,700,000 to 2,000,000 VND. Whether the week is credited, and whether the month is priced from the start of the trial, is exactly what the questions above are for. If nothing is credited, the trial costs about as much as the week itself; if the shop credits the week, it may cost much less. Treat these ranges as a yardstick, and get the actual figures in writing before the week begins.

Starting the trial well

Put the bike type you want, the dates of the week and the fact that you are trying the bike for a daily commute into one message, add the six questions above, and send it before day one. Keep the replies together with your booking details, so that the plan exists in writing.

To ask about converting the week, call 0334 699 969 between 09:00 and 21:00; the monthly rental page lists the shop's monthly rates and booking details.
